core_obligations: Localise and reduce to bounded above (proof lines 12287-12296): assume K + L is m-pseudo-coherent, pass to a covering over which K + L lies in D^- so that L does as well, and use the displayed distinguished triangle together with the cone lemma to get that L + L[1] is m-pseudo-coherent.

Shift and iterate (proof lines 12297-12303): the same argument makes L[1] + L[2] m-pseudo-coherent and, by induction, L[n] + L[n+1] for all n; since L is bounded above, L[n] is m-pseudo-coherent for large n.
Work backwards (proof lines 12304-12309): using the triangles (L[n], L[n] + L[n-1], L[n-1]) and the cone lemma again, m-pseudo-coherence descends from degree n to n-1 and finally to L.
proof_roadmap: Isolate L from the direct sum by a distinguished triangle and the cone lemma.
Shift to get L[n] + L[n+1] for all n and use boundedness above to start the descent.
Descend by the triangles (L[n], L[n] + L[n-1], L[n-1]) to reach L, and symmetrically K.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that m-pseudo-coherence passes to direct summands (statement lines 12279-12284). The proof (proof lines 12286-12309) isolates L by a distinguished triangle and the cone lemma, shifts to obtain L[n] + L[n+1] for all n, uses boundedness above to anchor the descent, and then works backwards through the triangles (L[n], L[n] + L[n-1], L[n-1]). H2: one triangle computation iterated along shifts.
